# Bundle Specification

Which of Link's programs to build from source, for which targets, and how to seal and sign them into one release folder. The `bundle` specification is TOML, given to a command that reads it as a file, and a field flag sets the field it names, overriding the file. Its JSON Schema is [`bundle.schema.json`](bundle.schema.json).

## Use It

Give `lnk bundle create` a `bundle` specification as a file, and set any field below with its field flag, which overrides the file. `lnk bundle spec show` prints the specification as it is read.

## Every Option

Every field the reader takes, with an example value.

```toml
kind = "bundle"
schema = 1
build = "dev"
components = ["../extra/modules/example"]
file = ["manifest.toml"]
from = ["part-linux"]
out = "dist"
outside = ["outside.toml"]
program = [
    "lnk",
    "lnk-box",
]
signer = "dev"
source = ["."]
target = ["x86_64-unknown-linux-musl"]
version = "0.14.0"
```

## `build`

> **Type** one of `dev`, `staging`, `prod` · **Flag** `--build`

Its stage, which says what its `lnk` trusts: `dev` (the bundle's own
signer and Link's), `staging` (the staging signer and Link's) or `prod`
(the bundle's own signer alone, at the workspace's version).

## `components`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--components`

A component folder, outside the built `lnk`'s own workspace, whose
module the bundle's `lnk` lists, repeated for more. Its commands then
answer on the machine the bundle installs to. A prod build lists it
only if it's released. It's none when none is given, whatever the
build's shell or folder says.

## `file`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--file`

A file sealed beside the programs, such as a manifest its installer
reads, repeated for more.

## `from`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--from`

Parts built before, unsigned, sealed instead of building, repeated for
each part.

## `out`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--out`

Where the bundle goes, `~/.lnk/data/bundles/<name>/<version>` when none is
given.

## `outside`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--outside`

A TOML file declaring programs Link doesn't build, such as Caddy,
repeated for more.

## `program`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--program`

A program to build, by its file name, such as `lnk-measure` or a program
of your own, repeated for more. It's `lnk` and every module of the first
source when none is given.

## `signer`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--signer`

Who signs it: `link`, `staging`, a signer of your own by name, kept in
`~/.lnk/safe/bundles/signers` and made on first use, or an
allowed-signers file. Dev and prod require a signer, including unsigned
parts that must embed its trust. Staging may omit it for unsigned parts.

## `source`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--source`

A workspace to find programs in, repeated for more. It's this folder
when none is given.

## `target`

> **Type** a list, each one of `host`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` · **Flag** `--target`

A target to build for, one of Link's release targets, such as
`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, or `host` for this computer's, repeated for
more. It's `host` when none is given.

- `host`: this computer's own target, one of the others
- `aarch64-apple-darwin`: macOS on arm64
- `x86_64-apple-darwin`: macOS on x86_64
- `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`: Linux on x86_64, built with musl so it needs no system libraries
- `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`: Linux on arm64, built with musl so it needs no system libraries

## `version`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--spec.version`

Its version. It's the workspace's, stamped for staging and dev, when
none is given.
